channel.title: Africanews RSS
channel.description: Receive free and in real-time all news published by africanews.com, by subscribing to our RSS feeds.

item.title: Cubans call for lifting of embargo, express hope for better lives
item.description: Cuban citizens expressed hope that the US will respond to the calls of the international community as soon as possible and voiced their wishes for better lives, after the United Nations General Assembly adopted a resolution for the 34th consecutive time urging the US to end its embargo.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: DRC: US sanctions on Rwanda draw mixed reactions in Goma
item.description: In Goma, some residents want to believe that this additional pressure could help break the deadlock. Michel Kamango hopes the sanctions will affect the parties concerned and help bring about a return to peace.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Putin hails 'natural allies' at Russia-Africa summit in Moscow
item.description: President Putin welcomed nearly two dozen African leaders to the Kremlin on Wednesday for a two-day Russia-Africa summit.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: Vatican: Century of Mercedes-Benz popemobiles goes on display
item.description: From silk-lined limousines to vehicles fitted with bulletproof glass, eight historic popemobiles go on display at the Vatican Museums. The exhibition traces how papal transport has evolved over nearly a century.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Alexis Caraco)

item.title: French music producer awaits trial six years after police beating
item.description: Six years after being violently beaten by three police officers, Michel Zecler is awaiting the opening of their trial on 9 November in Paris. The music producer says he remains deeply scarred and angry over police violence.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Gabon oil rig disaster: Three bodies found, two still missing
item.description: Three bodies have been found following the sinking of an oil rig off the coast of Gabon on Saturday, while the search continues for two people still missing, according to an updated toll released by Gabonese authorities overnight from Wednesday to Thursday.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: DRC Ebola clinic celebrates departure of last confirmed cases
item.description: Medical staff were joined by local residents as they celebrated the departure of the last Ebola patients from a treatment center in DR Congo’s Ituri province. It’s the first time the Médicins Sans Frontières-run clinic has had no confirmed Ebola cases since the outbreak was declared in May.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: A year after Tanzania’s bloody election, victims still await justice
item.description: A year after Tanzania's bloody election, many remain traumatised by the violence, while government critics live in fear of abduction and arbitrary arrest, or facing treason and terrorism charges.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Albania: opposition MPs disrupt parliament with smoke flares
item.description: Opposition MPs disrupted a parliamentary session in Albania by brandishing smoke flares and displaying photographs of injured protesters. They accused police of using violence against demonstrators demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Alexis Caraco)

item.title: Rembrandt's masterpieces become tattoos in the Netherlands
item.description: Visitors to the Rembrandt House Museum in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, can once again take home a piece of the Dutch master's art, permanently tattooed on their skin.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Alexis Caraco)

item.title: Pix of the Day, 29th October, 2026 - Across the world
item.description: Pix of the Day, 29th October, 2026 - Across the world
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Cameroonian opposition parties condemn the suspension of Issa Tchiroma’s party
item.description: Cameroonian opposition parties condemned the three-month suspension of Issa Tchiroma Bakary’s political party, the National Salvation Front of Cameroon.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Senegal: What strategies to tackle the debt? [Business Africa]
item.description: Senegal is stepping up negotiations with international creditors to ease its public debt burden, estimated at nearly 130% of GDP in 2025, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Yasmina El Abbasy)

item.title: Brazilians divided after defeated candidate Bolsonaro flees to US
item.description: As Brazilian media reported the news that defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro had fled to the US, public opinion remained divided. The 45-year-old former senator is under investigation over allegations of corruption, money laundering and tax evasion.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: Ghana says Russia has backed its bid to join BRICS as a partner country
item.description: Accra is seeking partner status in the bloc of emerging economies, hoping to attract investment, expand trade, and strengthen its economy.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Israel: protesters demand Arab-Jewish unity government after election
item.description: Protesters took to the streets of Tel Aviv to demand a government bringing together Jewish and Arab parties. With Israel's election producing no clear winner, police moved in to disperse activists blocking traffic.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Alexis Caraco)

item.title: Tunisian journalist sentenced to four years in jail on terrorism charges
item.description: International journalism organisations have condemned Zied el-Heni's conviction on terrorism offenses saying its an escalation of Tunisia's assault on the press.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Libya's eastern administration bans nationals from Iran and Afghanistan
item.description: Libya’s Government of National Stability that controls the country’s east has barred citizens of Iran and Afghanistan from entering its territory.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Spain: cranes clear twisted train wreckage as rescuers work through the night
item.description: Rescue teams worked through the night at the site of a train collision that killed 68 people near Toledo. Cranes continued clearing the wreckage as authorities set up a temporary morgue to identify victims.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Alexis Caraco)

item.title: 6 million in Haiti face severe hunger amid violence, displacement and El Niño
item.description: Aid organisations in Haiti are introducing a new programme to help people get enough to eat. Nearly six million people in the Caribbean nation are experiencing severe hunger, according to a new UN-backed report. Almost two million are facing emergency levels of food insecurity.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: US imposes sanctions on Rwandan defence ministry over links to Congo rebels
item.description: Washington hopes to increase pressure on Kigali to withdraw its troops from the DRC and end support for the M23 group.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Bahamas: King Charles III dances with locals during Caribbean visit
item.description: King Charles III showed off his dance moves during a colourful Junkanoo street parade in Nassau, the capital of the Bahamas, on Wednesday, 28 October, as part of his first Caribbean tour since becoming monarch.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Alexis Caraco)

item.title: Calls for slavery reparations grow louder as British king visits Caribbean
item.description: King Charles III's nine-day visit is being overshadowed by increasingly vocal demands for Britain to pay for its role in the slave trade.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Russia-Africa Summit: Putin seeks to expand ties with the continent
item.description: At the plenary session, Vladimir Putin told delegates that Moscow was Africa's best partner, calling for an end to Western domination.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Spain: Madrid mourns train crash victims as rescuers work through the night
item.description: Spain reels from the deadly Toledo high-speed train collision that killed 68 and injured more than 100, sparking grief, protests and calls for resignations.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Alexis Caraco)

item.title: Palestinian citizens of Israel hope election results bring change
item.description: Palestinian citizens of Israel expressed optimism on Wednesday following the strong showing of Arab parties in the elections.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Recreatrales festival transforms Ouagadougou neighbourhood
item.description: In Ouagadougou, an entire neighbourhood brings the Récréâtrales theatre festival to life. For its 14th edition, running from October 24 to 31, residents of Bougsemtenga are hosting performances in their courtyards.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Africa Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 cases, mostly in DR Congo
item.description: Africa's latest outbreak of Ebola has passed 10,000 confirmed cases, the vast majority of them in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Congolese health authorities said on Tuesday, with almost 5,000 fatalities.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: King Charles III's Caribbean tour renews calls for UK slavery reparations
item.description: The British king begins a tour of the Caribbean today, during which he will visit several former British colonies. It has renewed calls for the UK to apologies and pay reparations for its role in the slave trade.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Oil slick from Strait of Hormuz reaches UAE's northern coast
item.description: An oil slick from a tanker attacked in the Strait of Hormuz has reached the United Arab Emirates.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Spain: Rescuers search mangled train wreckage near Toledo
item.description: At least 68 people have been killed and dozens more injured after two high-speed trains collided near Urda, in central Spain’s Toledo province, on Wednesday, 28 October. Authorities warned the toll could rise further as rescuers searched the wreckage.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Alexis Caraco)

item.title: Humanitarian situation worsening in Sudan's camps for displaced people
item.description: Displaced and official at Al-Karama 3 camp in the city of El-Damazin in Sudan's Blue Nile state say the humanitarian conditions are deteriorating in the camp, as war rages in the country. "The camp hasn't received any food aid for four months now," says the camp's manager.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Bolsonaro’s son and family flee to Miami after refusing to concede
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro and his family landed in Miami on Monday after leaving Brazil, following his defeat in the presidential election.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Britain's King Charles III attends youth rally in the Bahamas
item.description: Britain’s King Charles III on Tuesday addressed a youth gathering at Clifford Park in Nassau, recalling the Bahamas’ independence celebrations in 1973 and highlighting the country’s cultural achievements and vulnerability to climate change.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: South Sudan independence figure Joseph Lagu dies aged 94
item.description: South Sudan is observing national mourning on Wednesday following the death of Joseph Lagu, a key figure in the independence of the world's youngest country, who told AFP that he began his fight armed with only "a machete".
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Tanzania announces first major natural gas discovery in a decade
item.description: Tanzania has announced its first natural gas discovery in a decade, with an estimated 223 billion cubic feet found at the Kasa-1X ST2 well in the Mnazi Bay area.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Pix of the Day, 28th October, 2026 - Across the world
item.description: Pix of the Day, 28th October, 2026 - Across the world
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: South African activists push back on data centre rush
item.description: Civil society groups have demanded a halt in the construction of new AI centres in South Africa. The prospect of a water- and power-hungry hyperscale data centre near areas of the city where thousands of people lack proper access to these resources has alarmed activists.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Russia's President Putin hosts counterparts from Mozambique, Libya and Equatorial Guinea
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin met for talks with counterparts from Mozambique, Libya and Equatorial Guinea in Moscow on Tuesday following the Gas Exporting Countries Forum.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Nigeria's Dangote oil refinery closes 'historic' IPO
item.description: Africa's largest ever initial public offering closed on Wednesday after raising funds from investors in 120 countries. The IPO for Nigeria's Dangote Petroleum Refinery was extended by two weeks to allow more Africans to participate.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Spain: First footage reveals wreckage of deadly high-speed train crash
item.description: At least 10 people died when a high-speed train struck another near Toledo, Spain. Two carriages derailed, leaving rescuers searching through the wreckage as authorities warned the death toll could rise.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Alexis Caraco)

item.title: Whereabouts of Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Bolsonaro unknown
item.description: The whereabouts of Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro were unknown on Wednesday after reports that he fled the country. Bolsonaro lost the runoff election to incumbent Luis Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday but has refused to concede defeat.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: No clear winner in Israel's first election since the 2023 Hamas attack
item.description: The vote has widely been seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s handling of the conflict, with turnout the highest in decades.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Judge throws out attempted murder case against Zimbabwe VP's ex-wife
item.description: After 7 years on remand, the ex-wife of Zimbabwe's vice president walked out of a Harare prison on Tuesday after a judge ordered her release. Marry Mubaiwa had been accused of attempting to murder her former husband Constantino Chiwenga in 2019.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Sana'a factory in flames as Houthis, government forces exchange strikes
item.description: Houthi media reported that Saudi-backed government forces have launched airstrikes on a "Hamdan" cement factory in Sana'a on Tuesday.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Brazil: Lula celebrates 81st birthday after re-election victory
item.description: Brazil's re-elected President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva celebrated his 81st birthday on Tuesday, 27 October, with dozens of supporters outside the Alvorada presidential palace in Brasília, just two days after winning a closely contested election.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Alexis Caraco)

item.title: Ukraine: massive fire engulfs buildings after Russian strike on Kharkiv
item.description: Five people, including a 4-year-old child, were injured in an overnight Russian drone strike on Kharkiv. The attack set several buildings ablaze, with firefighters working under the threat of further strikes.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Alexis Caraco)

item.title: Senegal's finance committee to review revised budget key to IMF deal
item.description: The country has been grappling with a debt burden that the IMF says had reached 132 per cent of gross domestic product by ⁠the end of 2024.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Iranian president says Middle East can solve its problems without United States
item.description: Masoud Pezeshkian made the comments during talks with Russia's President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum in Moscow.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Israel: opposition supporters celebrate narrow lead in exit polls
item.description: Supporters of Gadi Eisenkot celebrated in Tel Aviv as exit polls gave Israel's opposition bloc a narrow lead over Benjamin Netanyahu's camp, but no outright parliamentary majority.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Alexis Caraco)
